seen_animation: A black-line cannon (a capsule-shaped barrel over one spoked wheel) stands on a grey slab under clouds and plus-sign stars. In frame 1 the barrel points almost straight up and the wheel is a narrow vertical ellipse. Frames 2-5 tip the barrel down to the left until it lies diagonally across a rounder wheel. Frames 6-8 raise it back to vertical, with the wheel narrowing again. Frames 9-12 lower the barrel to the right, with the muzzle end at upper right and the wheel round. Frames 13-16 raise it back to near-vertical with a narrow wheel. The cannon stays over the centre of the slab and the slab does not change shape. The clouds slide sideways between frames.
seen_film: A model field gun on a square base turns a full 360 degrees on a turntable against a dark red starry background. Frame 1 shows it end-on, with both wheels visible and the barrel pointing at the camera. Frames 2-6 turn it until the barrel points to the upper left and the trail runs to the lower right. Frame 8 shows it end-on again, from the trail side. Frames 9-12 turn it so the barrel points to the upper right and the trail runs to the lower left. Frames 13-16 bring it back to an end-on view. The square base turns with the gun and drifts toward the lower right of the frame in frames 13-16.
evidence: Timing lines up with the film. In e.png the barrel points left in frames 4-10, while the film's gun points left in f.png frames 5-12. The animation's barrel is near-vertical in frames 14-16 and 29-32, when the film is end-on in f.png frames 15-16 and 30-32. It points right in frames 20-25, while the film points right in f.png frames 20-26. However, the animation shows the end-on views as the barrel standing straight up (e.png frames 1, 15, 16, 30, 31). The film shows them as a barrel foreshortened toward the camera between two wheels. So the animation reads as a cannon rocking or rearing up and down in the picture plane, not as a cannon spinning on a turntable. The grey slab stays a fixed flat rectangle in every frame (e.g. e.png 1, 8, 16, 24, 32), while the film's base visibly rotates and changes shape (f.png 1 vs 8 vs 15 vs 24). In f.png 25-32 the film's gun moves to the lower right of the frame, but the animated cannon stays centred (e.png 25-32). Motion between consecutive frames is continuous. g.png shows an unbroken arc from left-tilted to right-tilted, with no gaps or reversals. The only pops are scenery: cloud shapes duplicate and are clipped at the frame edges in frames 17-27.
primary_gap: The film's event is a 360-degree turn around a vertical axis, but the animation swings the barrel up and down in the picture plane, so the end-on views read as the cannon pointing at the sky instead of at the viewer.
closes_when: In the end-on frames (e.png 1, 15-16, 30-32), the barrel is drawn as a short foreshortened capsule pointing at the viewer, at or below wheel-top height, with its muzzle loop facing the camera. The slab also turns from a wide rectangle to a diamond and back, in step with the film's base.
protect: Keep the timing that matches the film (left-facing around frames 4-10, end-on around 15-16, right-facing around 20-25, end-on around 30-32). Keep the smooth frame-to-frame progression with no jumps. Keep the doodle's construction: a single capsule barrel with the closed loop at the breech, the open hooked stroke at the rear, and one ellipse wheel with crossing spoke strokes, all in the same thin black line.
identity_gap: The cannon keeps the doodle's capsule barrel, breech loop and crossed-spoke wheel, but the vertical end-on poses squash it into a tall narrow shape the doodle never shows.
